packageRules.description: The Go toolchain is pinned in go.mod (go directive, read by setup-go in both CI forges) and in the Dockerfile build stage. Move them in one PR so CI and the image never build with different compilers.
Bun is pinned in web/package.json packageManager (read by setup-bun in both CI forges) and in the Dockerfile web stage. Same reasoning as the Go toolchain.
golang.org/x/* release together and usually need to move together.
Routine frontend minor/patch bumps in one PR.
Keep the .gitea and .github copies of the same action on the same version.
sqlc is pinned in the Makefile (go run ...@vX) and in both CI workflows; move them together.

requires-python is the floor the project supports, not a dependency to pin: rangeStrategy pin made it ==3.14.8 while .python-version says 3.13, and uv sync refused in the hooks job. The interpreter is chosen by .python-version.

engines is the oldest Node the sync runner accepts, not a dependency to pin: rangeStrategy pin made it exactly v26.11.1 (#94) while the runner image runs Node 22. Same mistake as requires-python above.

The Node runtime is the runner image (integrations/rigel-sync/Dockerfile) and setup-node's node-version in both CI forges. Move them in one PR so CI tests the Node that ships; renovate offers only LTS majors here.
@types/node must describe the runtime's major, not the newest Node: #98 moved it to 26 under a Node 22 image. Its major moves by hand together with the node runtime group.

customManagers.description: Tool pins in the CI workflows are plain env strings that no other manager reads. The annotation sits on the line above the pin so it is obvious the value is managed.
